closingSelfCheck.summary: Independently ran both harnesses; every sizing/ceiling number and the exact ENOBUFS message text quoted in the summary match live output byte-for-byte, and all 10 git read sites carry the new maxBuffer. Both harnesses are genuinely registered in lattice.config.json (not merely present on disk), and the RED harness's differential is real (verbatim embedded pre-fix helper). CHK-004's 'accepted' verdict is honest, not overstated: it is outcome B under the checklist item's own definition ('ship the bounding OR commit a rationale naming the change that will'), backed by a thorough, self-critical decision document, and findings.json shows the four deferred findings closed as partially_mitigated (deferred-with-rationale), not silently marked fixed. The cross-vendor-codex and late-harness-registration pitfalls claims are corroborated in findings.json/review-passes.json (codex-tagged findings F-014-017, F-031/032, F-040/041 filed under agent 'main' then reproduced under Claude lanes; registration-only commit 5e65c6f330 confirmed by RP-015), and the LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS/effectiveEnvironmentDigest claim matches validation-command-environment.ts exactly (the variable is not in the transport-key exclusion list, so it is semantic to the digest). Two minor items I could not pin to the exact figure quoted, though neither contradicts the underlying point: the summary's 'a 40 MiB blob' description is an approximate paraphrase of a real repro in findings.json (not the committed harness's own 34,554,432-byte fixture, which produces the identical message because Node's partial capture stops shortly after the ceiling regardless of total blob size), and 'about 884 seconds' is lower than the 931,983 ms sum of per-command durations in the currently persisted test-evidence.json (both numbers are on the same side of, and consistent with, the 900000 ms watchdog needing to be raised).
